uw.history: Founded in 1848, UW–Madison grew into a public university guided by the Wisconsin Idea: knowledge should improve life beyond the campus.
uw.milestone: Its CS degree connects classroom learning with project courses, faculty research and a possible senior thesis.

waterloo.history: Waterloo opened in 1957 with 74 engineering students. Alternating study and work was part of its identity from the beginning.
waterloo.milestone: Hack the North brings builders together on campus. For a student who enjoys making things, it is a concrete example of the local project community.

gatech.history: Founded in 1885 to support industrial development, Georgia Tech has grown alongside Atlanta into a technological research university.
gatech.milestone: Its Threads approach connects computing to themes such as people, media, intelligence and systems, so students can shape a coherent area of study.

purdue.history: Purdue established the first computer science department in the United States in October 1962. The department helped define CS as its own academic discipline.
purdue.milestone: Today, a six-course core leads to specialized tracks. This combines a common technical foundation with room to choose advanced areas.

rit.history: RIT traces its roots to the Rochester Athenaeum of 1829 and the Mechanics Institute of 1885. Its current Henrietta campus opened in 1968.
rit.milestone: Its computing co-op model makes workplace experience part of the degree. CS is described as a five-year programme with three required co-op blocks.

asu.history: ASU began in 1885 as a school for teacher training, agriculture and mechanical arts. Its history reflects the growth of Arizona and its educational needs.
asu.milestone: The Tempe CS BS sits within the Fulton engineering schools and offers cybersecurity and software engineering concentrations.

cmu.history: Andrew Carnegie funded technical schools in Pittsburgh in 1900. In 1967, Carnegie Tech and the Mellon Institute merged to become Carnegie Mellon University.
cmu.milestone: CMU’s history connects computing and artificial intelligence with interdisciplinary work by Allen Newell and Herbert Simon.

uiuc.history: Illinois was founded in 1867 as a land-grant university. Its campus developed around a public mission of education and practical knowledge.
uiuc.milestone: NCSA Mosaic, released in 1993, helped bring the Web to a wider public. It is one of Illinois’s tangible contributions to computing history.

ubc.history: In 1922, UBC students organised the Great Trek to call for better facilities. The campaign is an important part of the university’s campus history.
ubc.milestone: The Vancouver campus sits at Point Grey. This profile refers to the Vancouver route; UBC Okanagan is a different campus.

uoft.history: The University of Toronto was central to the discovery and early development of insulin. Its library preserves records of the work from 1920–1925.
uoft.milestone: St. George is the downtown campus, close to research hospitals and entrepreneurship hubs. Scarborough has its own campus and programme route.

utsc.history: Toronto Scarborough was founded in 1964. It moved to its present site when the original buildings opened in January 1966.
utsc.milestone: Its park-like campus is on Toronto’s eastern edge. Studying here is a different campus experience from downtown St. George.

manchester.history: On 21 June 1948, the Manchester Baby ran a program stored electronically in its memory. It was a landmark in the history of modern computing.
manchester.milestone: The Baby was followed by the Manchester Mark I and the Ferranti Mark I, connecting experimental computing with practical machines.
